correctness.rationale: The exact commutator reduces every pairwise ordering comparison to a quadratic with a strictly positive rational denominator. A sign argument proves at most one positive switch, and strict monotonicity of every unit propagates adjacent pairwise improvements. These steps prove the universal order iff theorem and the high/low global sort limits. A symbolic identity, an exact rational switch witness, 10,000 seeded comparisons and 133 exhaustive exact-rational permutation sets independently checked critical identities, without treating finite tests as a universal proof.

The nutrient-spiraling synthesis and first-order effective-removal scaling analysis address different objectives. The closest full-text-unavailable 1994 reaction-chain article concerns linearized transfer functions; it remains a stated risk, as do abstract general monotone-map interchange theorems. This is a best-knowledge provisional mathematical originality assessment, not historical certification.

value.rationale: Serial reach arrangement under saturation is identified as an important biogeochemical question by the original 2010 study. The exact all-input existence iff criterion, differing extreme-input sorted permutations, and unique two-reach switching concentration give a complete structural answer within a clearly delimited mathematical model. These statements are more informative than a single easy numerical counterexample or a reparameterization, but do not imply real-stream engineering recommendations or an intermediate-concentration global sorting theorem.
